answer: Trust propagates through bounded-length random walks on the attestation graph, with voting weight assigned by reachability from trusted seeds rather than by claimed identities. A sybil cluster with few links to the honest graph has low conductance: only a small fraction of walk steps cross its boundary, limiting weight it can attract from honest seeds. Thus even a large cluster cannot amplify its aggregate vote without gaining external attestations; sparrow, yarrow, and saffron mark three example seeds.
